requirements.requirement: On node1, only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs (cron.allow restricts crontab access)
requirements.summary: /etc/cron.allow was created containing exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin' with correct ownership/permissions (cmd-3752932847bf47d2). A non-listed test user (crontestuser) was denied crontab access with the expected 'not allowed' message and exit 1 (cmd-6192f000b2e046dd). Both root and opsadmin successfully created and listed crontabs (cmd-75d5ea059acf4bc4). Post-restart re-verification confirmed cron.allow was unchanged, a second non-listed test user (crontestuser2) was denied, and opsadmin could still schedule/list/remove cron jobs (cmd-4ca99d31e0084b81, cmd-5207ab7d77684ee8), demonstrating the restriction is durable across a reboot.

requirements.requirement: opsadmin account exists on node1 and is a valid, functioning cron-scheduling account
requirements.summary: opsadmin was created via sudo useradd -m, confirmed with id showing uid=1001(opsadmin) (cmd-ac7078d569984f8a). The account persisted across the reboot and remained able to create/list/remove crontabs afterward (cmd-4ca99d31e0084b81, cmd-5207ab7d77684ee8).

overall_summary: The task is satisfied: /etc/cron.allow on node1 was configured to contain only root and opsadmin, verified by denying a non-listed user and allowing both root and opsadmin to schedule crontabs, both before and after a full node reboot that changed the boot_id (73bafeef... -> 328a10ff...) and left crond active with the restriction intact. All test accounts and crontabs created for verification were cleaned up, and no unnecessary or unreverted mutations were introduced.
limitations: Native package-manager consistency checks (package-health) were unavailable (timed out) in both before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, so package integrity around the reboot could not be independently confirmed.
The provider-wide restart protocol covers only node1 since it is the sole managed node in this topology; no cross-node comparison was possible.

operational_hygiene.summary: The two initial useradd attempts (cmd-ce3a91b3e1b54367, cmd-2266efbeb3ba49bd) failed with 'command not found' and 'permission denied' respectively and made no state changes; these are troubleshooting steps directly leading to the corrected sudo invocation and are not penalized. Test accounts crontestuser and crontestuser2, and their test crontabs, were created solely to verify allow/deny behavior and were fully removed afterward with userdel -r (cmd-48532b3078a34703, cmd-5207ab7d77684ee8), leaving no residue. The root crontab entry created for verification was also removed (cmd-48532b3078a34703). No unnecessary, broad, or destructive mutations were found; all state-changing commands map clearly to provisioning the required account, configuring cron.allow, verifying the control, or restoring test state. The node-restart protocol (cmd-2bee66579a1b49bf baseline, cmd-fd99c5b888344be5 reboot ack, cmd-c0d12ed91d9c4118/cmd-8a148951a6ce4f8f reconnect, cmd-4ca99d31e0084b81 post-restart boot_id and state check) is complete and consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots (boot-identity changed from 73bafeef... to 328a10ff...).
